evidence.quote: today the FOMC raised its policy interest rate by ¾ of a percentage point and anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range for the federal funds rate will be appropriate.

As the stance of monetary policy tightens further, it likely will become appropriate to slow the pace of increases while we assess how our cumulative policy adjustments are affecting the economy and inflation.
The labor market is extremely tight, and inflation is much too high.
Recent indicators of spending and production have softened.
Inflation has obviously surprised to the upside over the past year, and further surprises could be in store.
we are continuing the process of significantly reducing the size of our balance sheet.

parsed.rationale: A 75bp hike, continued runoff, forceful inflation concern and expectations of ongoing increases toward a moderately restrictive level are clearly hawkish. Signals that the pace will eventually slow, the move to meeting-by-meeting guidance, and acknowledged softening in activity temper the stance.
